1	# Developer Workforce & Compensation Trends — 2024 Stack Overflow Survey
2	
3	## Source
4	https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work
5	
6	## Employment Status
7	
8	84% of the 65,437 respondents are currently working (full-time, part-time, or freelancing). Full-time employment is the dominant mode at 69%, followed by independent contracting/freelancing at 16.4% and full-time students at 13.2%.
9	
10	In the United States specifically, full-time employment dropped from 69% in 2023 to 64.8% in 2024. In the U.K. and Ukraine, non-full-time respondents lean toward independent contracting, while in Germany and India they are more likely to be full-time students.
11	
12	## Work Environment Trends
13	
14	Hybrid work remains the most common arrangement at 42%, consistent with 2023. Remote work accounts for 38%. In-person work has risen for the third consecutive year — from 15% in 2022 to 16% in 2023 to 20% in 2024 — signaling a gradual return-to-office trend.
15	
16	## Company Size
17	
18	47% of respondents work for organizations with fewer than 100 employees. The distribution across 42,827 respondents:
19	
20	| Company Size | Share |
21	|---|---|
22	| Freelancer / solo | 6.1% |
23	| 2–9 employees | 10.4% |
24	| 10–19 employees | 8.9% |
25	| 20–99 employees | 21.2% |
26	| 100–499 employees | 18.5% |
27	| 500–999 employees | 6.7% |
28	| 1,000–4,999 employees | 11.0% |
29	| 5,000–9,999 employees | 3.8% |
30	| 10,000+ employees | 11.4% |
31	
32	## Salary by Developer Type
33	
34	Median annual compensation (USD, all respondents) varies dramatically by role. The top and bottom roles are shown below (22,677 salary responses, 34.7% response rate):
35	
36	| Developer Type | Median Salary (USD) | Avg. Years Experience |
37	|---|---|---|
38	| Senior Executive | $127,388 | ~17 |
39	| Dev Advocate | $124,203 | ~16 |
40	| Manager | $115,999 | ~15 |
41	| Dev Experience | $109,483 | ~12 |
42	| SRE | $99,099 | ~10 |
43	| Cloud Infra. Engineer | $96,666 | ~13 |
44	| Blockchain | $85,925 | ~9 |
45	| Product Manager | $80,000 | ~14 |
46	| Full-stack | $63,333 | ~10 |
47	| Front-end | $48,787 | ~8 |
48	| Student | $15,466 | ~2 |
49	
50	Site reliability engineers and cloud infrastructure engineers are the highest-paid purely technical roles, reflecting their critical importance in keeping digital services running. Regionally, mobile developers earn more in the U.S., data engineers top the charts in Germany and Ukraine, and back-end developers lead in India and the U.K.
51	
52	![Salary by developer type — bar chart](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
53	
54	![Salary vs. experience by developer type — scatter plot](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
55	
56	## Salary by Programming Language
57	
58	Developers using niche functional languages earn the most. The overall reported salary range has dropped roughly $10K compared to 2023, now averaging $60–75K USD vs. $70–85K USD last year.
59	
60	| Language | Median Salary (USD) | Avg. Years Experience |
61	|---|---|---|
62	| Erlang | ~$97,000 | ~12 |
63	| Clojure | ~$95,000 | ~11 |
64	| Elixir | ~$93,000 | ~11 |
65	| Perl | ~$90,000 | ~19 |
66	| Ruby | ~$89,000 | ~11 |
67	| Scala | ~$88,000 | ~9 |
68	| Go | ~$76,000 | ~9 |
69	| Python | ~$67,000 | ~9 |
70	| JavaScript | ~$64,000 | ~10 |
71	| PHP | ~$49,000 | ~10 |
72	| Dart | ~$44,000 | ~8 |
73	| Prolog | ~$43,000 | ~9 |
74	
75	![Salary vs. experience by language — scatter plot](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
76	
77	## Technology Purchasing Influence
78	
79	62% of respondents have influence over technology purchases at their organizations. Senior executives (99%), engineering managers (87%), and product managers (77%) wield the most influence. 60% of respondents prefer a build-and-buy approach over purely building or buying. Starting a free trial (75%) and asking other developers (73%) are the top methods for evaluating new tools.
80	
81	## Key Findings
82	
83	- **Full-time employment is softening**: U.S. full-time employment fell 4 percentage points year-over-year; freelancing and contracting remain significant at 16%+.
84	- **In-person work is creeping back**: now at 20%, up from 15% in 2022, though hybrid (42%) still dominates.
85	- **DevRel and leadership roles command premium pay**: Senior Executives ($127K), Dev Advocates ($124K), and Managers ($116K) top the salary chart, all with 15+ years average experience.
86	- **Niche functional languages correlate with higher pay**: Erlang, Clojure, and Elixir developers earn >$93K median, while mainstream languages like JavaScript and PHP sit well below $65K.
87	- **Developers are key purchase influencers**: with 62% having a say in tech buying decisions, vendor strategies should target individual contributors, not just management.

"""Build an 8-slide 16:9 PPTX deck on 2024 Stack Overflow Developer Survey data."""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE, XL_LEGEND_POSITION, XL_LABEL_POSITION
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData, XyChartData
import os

# ── Constants ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SLIDE_W = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_H = Inches(7.5)
DARK_BG = RGBColor(0x1B, 0x1F, 0x2B)
ACCENT_BLUE = RGBColor(0x3B, 0x82, 0xF6)
ACCENT_TEAL = RGBColor(0x14, 0xB8, 0xA6)
ACCENT_ORANGE = RGBColor(0xF5, 0x9E, 0x0B)
ACCENT_PURPLE = RGBColor(0xA7, 0x8B, 0xFA)
ACCENT_RED = RGBColor(0xEF, 0x44, 0x44)
WHITE = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GRAY = RGBColor(0x94, 0xA3, 0xB8)
MID_GRAY = RGBColor(0x64, 0x74, 0x8B)
CARD_BG = RGBColor(0x24, 0x2A, 0x38)

ASSETS = "/app/benchmark/assets"
OUTPUT = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"

prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = SLIDE_W
prs.slide_height = SLIDE_H
blank_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank


def add_dark_bg(slide):
    bg = slide.background
    fill = bg.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BG


def add_text_box(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                 bold=False, color=WHITE, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                 font_name="Calibri", line_spacing=None):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = alignment
    if line_spacing:
        p.line_spacing = Pt(line_spacing)
    return txBox


def add_rounded_rect(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color=CARD_BG):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    shape.shadow.inherit = False
    return shape


def add_accent_line(slide, left, top, width, color=ACCENT_BLUE):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, Pt(4))
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape


def add_stat_card(slide, left, top, width, height, number, label, accent=ACCENT_BLUE):
    card = add_rounded_rect(slide, left, top, width, height)
    add_accent_line(slide, left + Inches(0.2), top + Inches(0.15), Inches(0.6), accent)
    add_text_box(slide, left + Inches(0.2), top + Inches(0.35), width - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.6),
                 number, font_size=28, bold=True, color=accent)
    add_text_box(slide, left + Inches(0.2), top + Inches(0.9), width - Inches(0.4), Inches(0.6),
                 label, font_size=13, color=LIGHT_GRAY)


def add_slide_number(slide, num, total=8):
    add_text_box(slide, SLIDE_W - Inches(1.2), SLIDE_H - Inches(0.5),
                 Inches(1), Inches(0.3), f"{num} / {total}",
                 font_size=10, color=MID_GRAY, alignment=PP_ALIGN.RIGHT)


# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE 1 — Title
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
slide1 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
add_dark_bg(slide1)

add_accent_line(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(2.0), Inches(2), ACCENT_BLUE)

add_text_box(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(2.3), Inches(10), Inches(1.2),
             "Developer Workforce &\nCompensation Trends",
             font_size=40, bold=True, color=WHITE, line_spacing=48)

add_text_box(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(3.8), Inches(10), Inches(0.5),
             "2024 Stack Overflow Developer Survey",
             font_size=22, color=ACCENT_BLUE)

add_text_box(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(4.6), Inches(10), Inches(0.5),
             "65,437 respondents  •  180+ countries  •  2024",
             font_size=16, color=LIGHT_GRAY)

add_text_box(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(5.5), Inches(10), Inches(0.4),
             "Source: survey.stackoverflow.co/2024/work",
             font_size=12, color=MID_GRAY)

# Decorative dots
for i, c in enumerate([ACCENT_BLUE, ACCENT_TEAL, ACCENT_ORANGE]):
    dot = slide1.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.OVAL,
                                  Inches(10.5) + Inches(i * 0.5), Inches(2.3),
                                  Inches(0.3), Inches(0.3))
    dot.fill.solid()
    dot.fill.fore_color.rgb = c
    dot.line.fill.background()

add_slide_number(slide1, 1)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE 2 — Employment Status
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)

add_text_box(slide2, Inches(0.8), Inches(0.4), Inches(11), Inches(0.7),
             "84% of Developers Are Working, but Full-Time Employment Dips in the U.S.",
             font_size=26, bold=True, color=WHITE)
add_accent_line(slide2, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.05), Inches(1.5), ACCENT_BLUE)

# Global stats cards
add_stat_card(slide2, Inches(0.8), Inches(1.5), Inches(2.6), Inches(1.7),
              "69%", "Full-Time Employment\n(Global)", ACCENT_BLUE)

              "16.4%", "Independent / Freelance\n(Global)", ACCENT_TEAL)

              "13.2%", "Full-Time Students\n(Global)", ACCENT_ORANGE)
add_stat_card(slide2, Inches(9.5), Inches(1.5), Inches(2.6), Inches(1.7),
              "84%", "Currently Working\n(Any capacity)", ACCENT_PURPLE)

# US comparison card
us_card = add_rounded_rect(slide2, Inches(0.8), Inches(3.7), Inches(5.5), Inches(3.2))
add_accent_line(slide2, Inches(1.0), Inches(3.85), Inches(0.8), ACCENT_RED)
add_text_box(slide2, Inches(1.0), Inches(4.1), Inches(5), Inches(0.4),
             "U.S. Full-Time Employment Trend", font_size=16, bold=True, color=WHITE)

# Grouped bar chart for US comparison
chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ['2023', '2024']
chart_data.add_series('Full-Time %', (69.0, 64.8))

chart_frame = slide2.shapes.add_chart(
    XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED, Inches(1.0), Inches(4.6),
    Inches(4.8), Inches(2.1), chart_data
)
chart = chart_frame.chart
chart.has_legend = False
plot = chart.plots[0]
plot.gap_width = 120
series = plot.series[0]
series.format.fill.solid()
series.format.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT_RED

cat_axis = chart.category_axis
cat_axis.tick_labels.font.size = Pt(11)
cat_axis.tick_labels.font.color.rgb = LIGHT_GRAY
cat_axis.format.line.fill.background()

val_axis = chart.value_axis
val_axis.minimum_scale = 60
val_axis.maximum_scale = 72
val_axis.tick_labels.font.size = Pt(10)
val_axis.tick_labels.font.color.rgb = LIGHT_GRAY
val_axis.format.line.fill.background()
val_axis.major_gridlines.format.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x33, 0x3A, 0x4A)

chart.chart_style = 2
chart_frame.chart.element.getparent().getparent()

# Add data labels
for point_idx in range(2):
    point = series.points[point_idx]
    point.data_label.font.size = Pt(12)
    point.data_label.font.color.rgb = WHITE
    point.data_label.font.bold = True
    point.data_label.number_format = '0.0"%"'
    point.data_label.show_value = True

# Regional insight card
regional = add_rounded_rect(slide2, Inches(6.8), Inches(3.7), Inches(5.5), Inches(3.2))
add_accent_line(slide2, Inches(7.0), Inches(3.85), Inches(0.8), ACCENT_TEAL)
add_text_box(slide2, Inches(7.0), Inches(4.1), Inches(5), Inches(0.4),
             "Regional Patterns", font_size=16, bold=True, color=WHITE)

bullets = [

    ("Germany & India:", "Non-FT respondents are more\nlikely to be full-time students"),

for i, (title, desc) in enumerate(bullets):

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE 3 — Work Environment Shift

add_text_box(slide3, Inches(0.8), Inches(0.4), Inches(11), Inches(0.7),

colors3 = [ACCENT_BLUE, ACCENT_TEAL, ACCENT_ORANGE]

    ("Remote Declining", "38%", "Down from 45%\nin 2022", ACCENT_BLUE),

for i, (title, val, desc, accent) in enumerate(insights):

    card = add_rounded_rect(slide3, Inches(8.8), y, Inches(3.8), Inches(1.5))
    add_accent_line(slide3, Inches(9.0), y + Inches(0.15), Inches(0.5), accent)
    add_text_box(slide3, Inches(9.0), y + Inches(0.35), Inches(3.5), Inches(0.3),
                 title, font_size=13, bold=True, color=WHITE)
    add_text_box(slide3, Inches(9.0), y + Inches(0.6), Inches(1.2), Inches(0.4),
                 val, font_size=24, bold=True, color=accent)
    add_text_box(slide3, Inches(10.2), y + Inches(0.65), Inches(2.4), Inches(0.6),
                 desc, font_size=11, color=LIGHT_GRAY)

add_slide_number(slide3, 3)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE 4 — Salary by Developer Type (horizontal bar chart)
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
slide4 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
add_dark_bg(slide4)

add_text_box(slide4, Inches(0.8), Inches(0.4), Inches(11), Inches(0.7),
             "Senior Executives and Dev Advocates Top $124K+ Median Salary",
             font_size=26, bold=True, color=WHITE)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Build an 8-slide 16:9 PPTX deck on 2024 Stack Overflow Developer Survey data."""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE, XL_LEGEND_POSITION, XL_LABEL_POSITION
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData, XyChartData
import os

# ── Constants ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SLIDE_W = Inches(13.333)
SLIDE_H = Inches(7.5)
DARK_BG = RGBColor(0x1B, 0x1F, 0x2B)
ACCENT_BLUE = RGBColor(0x3B, 0x82, 0xF6)
ACCENT_TEAL = RGBColor(0x14, 0xB8, 0xA6)
ACCENT_ORANGE = RGBColor(0xF5, 0x9E, 0x0B)
ACCENT_PURPLE = RGBColor(0xA7, 0x8B, 0xFA)
ACCENT_RED = RGBColor(0xEF, 0x44, 0x44)
WHITE = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GRAY = RGBColor(0x94, 0xA3, 0xB8)
MID_GRAY = RGBColor(0x64, 0x74, 0x8B)
CARD_BG = RGBColor(0x24, 0x2A, 0x38)

ASSETS = "/app/benchmark/assets"
OUTPUT = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"

prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = SLIDE_W
prs.slide_height = SLIDE_H
blank_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank


def add_dark_bg(slide):
    bg = slide.background
    fill = bg.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = DARK_BG


def add_text_box(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=18,
                 bold=False, color=WHITE, alignment=PP_ALIGN.LEFT,
                 font_name="Calibri", line_spacing=None):
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = Pt(font_size)
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.color.rgb = color
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = alignment
    if line_spacing:
        p.line_spacing = Pt(line_spacing)
    return txBox


def add_rounded_rect(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color=CARD_BG):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height)
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    shape.shadow.inherit = False
    return shape


def add_accent_line(slide, left, top, width, color=ACCENT_BLUE):
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, left, top, width, Pt(4))
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = color
    shape.line.fill.background()
    return shape


def add_stat_card(slide, left, top, width, height, number, label, accent=ACCENT_BLUE):
